name: cstar-forge
raw_meta_yaml:
# rattler-build (v1) recipe for cstar-forge.

schema_version: 1

context:
  version: "0.6.0"
  python_min: "3.12"

package:
  name: cstar-forge
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  url: https://pypi.org/packages/source/c/cstar-forge/cstar_forge-${{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: 76b3af13c8c59f59b2d4cced2bba36e582328f6792d4c85cf0933e112ad88369

build:
  number: 0
  # note: we expect windows builds to fail due to a downstream dependency (xesmf)
  # not being available for windows. we still use noarch and accept the windows
  # build failures based on previous conda-forge admin guidance.
  noarch: python
  script:
    - python -m pip install . -vv --no-deps --no-build-isolation
    # Ship activate.d/deactivate.d hooks (recipe/activate.sh has the full
    # rationale) that set PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1 on env activation, keeping the
    # env off Python's user-site (~/.local) — which otherwise precedes the
    # env's site-packages on sys.path and silently shadows it, a chronic
    # breakage on HPC systems where a module Python shares ~/.local.
    # .sh only: this is a noarch package, but the hooks target HPC/Linux/macOS;
    # on Windows they are simply inert.
    - mkdir -p "$PREFIX/etc/conda/activate.d" "$PREFIX/etc/conda/deactivate.d"
    - cp "$RECIPE_DIR/activate.sh" "$PREFIX/etc/conda/activate.d/cstar-forge_pythonnousersite.sh"
    - cp "$RECIPE_DIR/deactivate.sh" "$PREFIX/etc/conda/deactivate.d/cstar-forge_pythonnousersite.sh"

requirements:
  host:
    - python ${{ python_min }}.*
    - pip
    - setuptools >=64
    - setuptools-scm >=8
  run:
    - python >=${{ python_min }}
    # -- mirrors [project.dependencies] in pyproject.toml --
    - jinja2
    - pandas
    - pyyaml >=6.0
    - copernicusmarine
    - gdown
    - dask
    - distributed
    - threadpoolctl
    - fsspec
    - pydantic
    - numpy
    - xarray
    - nbformat
    - psutil
    # typer backs the `cstar forge ...` CLI subcommand group (cstar_forge/cli.py);
    # it currently only arrives transitively.
    - typer
    - kerchunk
    - nest-asyncio
    - ujson
    - fastparquet
    - cstar-ocean >=0.12.0
    - roms-tools >=4.1.1,<5
    # -- the `app` extra, bundled deliberately (batteries-included conda
    # package, matching the roms-tools metapackage philosophy): the blueprint
    # wizard runs under voila/jupyter out of the box --
    - jupyterlab
    - voila
    - papermill
    - ipywidgets
    # matplotlib-base (not the `matplotlib` GUI metapackage): notebooks render
    # via the inline/Agg backends; keeps pyqt out of the default install.
    - matplotlib-base
  run_constraints:
    # copernicusmarine 2.4.x's conda-forge package under-pins click
    # (>=8.0.4,<8.3) relative to its own wheel metadata (>8.2.0,!=8.3.0,
    # !=8.3.1), so an unconstrained solve can pick click 8.1.x and fail
    # `pip check`. Constrain to the intersection; drop once the
    # copernicusmarine feedstock aligns its pin.
    - click >8.2.0,<8.3.0

tests:
  - python:
      imports:
        - cstar_forge
      pip_check: true
      python_version:
        - ${{ python_min }}.*
        - "*"

about:
  homepage: https://github.com/CWorthy-ocean/cstar-forge
  summary: Generates regional oceanographic modeling domains and reproducible C-Star workflows
  description: |
    C-STAR Forge generates regional oceanographic modeling domains and
    reproducible C-Star workflows. It automates the creation of ROMS-MARBL
    domains by producing all required input files (grids, initial conditions,
    forcing, boundaries, rivers, tidal forcing) from observational and
    reanalysis datasets.
  license: Apache-2.0
  license_file: LICENSE

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - ScottEilerman
